tldr: Anthropic reportedly told investors Q3 revenue hit $16.8B (from $11.6B in Q2) with an 85% adjusted gross margin, ahead of an IPO targeting up to $2T; the same day the FTC served civil subpoenas on Anthropic and OpenAI over AI safety incidents and NYC's comptroller urged Anthropic to pause its listing.
Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816B-parameter (42B active) open-weight model with 1M context that Apple says runs locally on two 512GB M5 Ultra Mac Studios.

In China, DeepSeek suffered a roughly five-hour API outage (08:11-13:04 Beijing time) and will refund 7 days of API spend as credits; StepFun open-sourced its 600B-parameter Step 5 Preview with day-0 Huawei Ascend, MetaX and Biren support.

items.title: Anthropic tells investors Q3 revenue hit $16.8B, adjusted profitable, as IPO nears
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly told prospective investors that third-quarter revenue reached $16.8 billion, up from $11.6 billion in Q2 and about $4.7 billion in Q1, and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis. Bloomberg cites an adjusted gross margin of 85% and notes the quarter's growth was under 50% from June, a marked deceleration. Anthropic is expected to begin marketing its IPO in early November at a valuation of up to $2 trillion, with a debut no later than year-end.
items.why_it_matters: The numbers anchor what would be the largest IPO ever and are being read as a test for the whole AI trade. Slowing sequential growth and a stalled IPO calendar frame the risk.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, an 816B-parameter open-weight model, and runs it on Macs with Apple
items.summary: Meta released Muse Spark Open, an open-weight multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 816B total and 42B active parameters and a 1M-token context window, aimed at coding and agentic work. Weights are on Hugging Face, Amazon SageMaker, Google Cloud Model Garden and Microsoft Foundry. Meta and Apple said it can run locally on two 512GB M5 Ultra Mac Studios using MLX, and NVIDIA published a guide to serving it on GB300 NVL72.
items.why_it_matters: It is Meta's first open-weight Muse model at frontier scale and is pitched as the strongest US open-weight model, pressuring Chinese open-weight leaders. The Apple tie-up makes local use of a model this size plausible.

items.title: FTC sends civil subpoenas to Anthropic and OpenAI in AI safety-incident probe
items.summary: The FTC sent civil investigative demands to Anthropic and OpenAI on Oct 14, an agency spokesperson confirmed to The Hill. Axios, citing a person familiar, says each runs 50+ pages covering security incidents, safeguarding practices, marketing materials and privacy policies. The probe, first reported Sept 30 as industry-wide and including evaluator METR, is expected to extend to executive testimony and third-party AI organizations.
items.why_it_matters: It moves the first federal consumer-protection probe of frontier-lab safety from reported inquiry to compulsory process, days before Anthropic's planned IPO marketing.

items.title: NYC Comptroller Levine urges Anthropic to pause IPO over AI safety and governance
items.summary: New York City Comptroller Mark Levine sent Anthropic a letter dated Oct 14 asking it to put AI safety and governance ahead of going public, arguing IPO preparation diverts resources from safety work. The letter cites Dario Amodei's Sept 12 essay calling for slower capability development and the draft S-1's reported catastrophic-risk warning, and asks for a written response with a timeline for audits and controls. The comptroller's office has no direct power over the offering.
items.why_it_matters: A major public-pension steward publicly pressing a pause adds institutional pressure just as the largest-ever IPO is being marketed.

items.title: Anthropic gives METR employee-level access and waives veto over publication of its findings
items.summary: Anthropic has given six METR researchers employee-level access (company laptops, office space, internal tools) to evaluate its models, incidents and practices. TechCrunch reports Anthropic waived its right to block METR publications, with removal requests limited to narrow categories such as customer data and model architecture details. Reuters adds Anthropic is also working with SecureBio and Accenture's Faculty in a three-tier evaluator scheme.
items.why_it_matters: It is the most concrete step yet toward embedded third-party evaluation of a frontier lab, after weeks of agent-incident disclosures.

items.title: TSMC posts sixth straight record quarterly profit; chip capacity a 'fierce' battleground
items.summary: TSMC reported Q3 net profit of NT$763.1B, up 68.7% year on year and above the NT$746.3B expected, on revenue of NT$1.49T (about $46.4B). Operating margin was 58.7%, above the top of guidance, and the company raised its full-year revenue outlook. A companion CNBC report says Nvidia, Apple, AMD and Broadcom are in an 'extremely fierce' fight for TSMC capacity; TSMC is also assessing whether customers have the financing to deploy AI systems.
items.why_it_matters: TSMC remains the binding supply constraint for AI silicon, and its demand read-through lands during an AI funding scare.

items.title: Mistral releases Timestral, its first time-series foundation models, in four sizes up to 209M
items.summary: Mistral released Timestral, zero-shot probabilistic forecasting models at 5M, 28M, 123M and 209M parameters. Mistral says the 209M model ranks first on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench, and the 28M model beats the roughly 4x larger Chronos-2 on GIFT-Eval and TIME. The models run on CPU, support up to 32K-step context, and ship as open weights under a Modified MIT license.
items.why_it_matters: It takes Mistral beyond language models into forecasting, where small CPU-friendly models are the draw.

items.title: Chinese team proves 3D Ghys conjecture with Shanghai AI Lab's Intern-S2 model, formally verified
items.original_title: 中国科学家首次用中国大模型攻克世界级数学难题，曾困扰学界30余年
items.summary: IT之家 reports that a team led by Xu Disheng (Great Bay University, visiting scholar at Shanghai AI Laboratory) used the lab's Intern-S2 science multimodal model, working with humans, to prove the three-dimensional Ghys conjecture, an open dynamical-systems problem posed in 1995. A Peking University team formally verified the proof with its SHEAF framework. The paper is on arXiv and the formalisation code is on GitHub.
items.why_it_matters: A headline claim of a Chinese LLM contributing to a long-open maths problem, with formal verification behind it, which is rarer than informal AI proofs.
